answers.text: The rule I'd keep: three lines every time, in order — drop-off time, pallet count, then any damage noted, with 'none noted' if there wasn't any. If something's missing, say no time given, I'd put 'not given' rather than making one up. It comes out the same each time because the three lines are always there.

Tell it: list only the calls flagged as needing follow-up, one line each — time, customer, topic — then a count at the top that's just how many lines are in that list. If two lines look like the same call logged twice, count it once and note 'duplicate, counted once' rather than listing it twice.

The note doesn't add up on the finishing time: access is from 8am on the 22nd, six hours from there finishes early afternoon the same day, not the 23rd like it says. That's a day out. I'd want it checked before it's filed.
9 out of 118 late is close enough to the 92% they gave, so that part is right. But 96 up to 118 is nearer 23%, not the 20% written.

I'd sign off the second one, it shows 940 and 827 and the working, so you can see where 88% comes from. The first is just the number by itself — if it were wrong there'd be nothing in the sentence to show it. Could well be correct, it's just not checkable as it stands.

I'd send the second email, the volumes and the PO log reference are right there so the 1,200 to 1,650 can be checked against something. The first just says 'we'd expect a better rate' with nothing behind it, so that line can't be checked as written. Not wrong as such, it would just need the numbers put behind it before it goes.
1. Yes. 2. Yes. 3. No. 4. Yes, already public. 5. No, personal address.

The hourly rates and retainer cap I wouldn't paste straight in, that's the sensitive commercial bit. The non-disclosure clause too, since it names both companies. The general service scope is fine to include as it is, nothing sensitive about what work is covered.
I'd check a few of the depot totals against the warehouse records directly, before the summary goes to finance.

Step 4 is where I'd put the gate, since once the payment note goes out automatically there's no easy way to pull it back. Step 1 matters too, a wrong figure from the PDF carries through everything that follows, but it's step 4 where it turns into an actual payment.
